alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 1 at 11:59PM EST until November 2 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
alerts.description:
An upper level low will will continue to influence storms in the
Gulf and Bahamas through Monday. With the lack of a strong synoptic
surface forcing mechanism, predictability as to where and when heavy
rain will fall remains low. However, the environment continues to
support the potential for heavy rainfall and slow moving cells.

* WHAT...Heavy rain may cause, or worsen ongoing urban and street
flooding.

* WHERE...All of South Florida

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Isolated to scattered areas of flash flooding will be
possible, with the main impact being street flooding, road
closures, and limited impact to structures in flood prone areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Pockets of very heavy rainfall resulted in localized flash
flooding on Sunday and those areas, and others, have the
potential to be impacted again on Monday. Forecast amounts look
very similar to yesterday,

700 AM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Western Atlantic:
An area of low pressure is likely to form along a weakening frontal 
boundary a few hundred miles northeast of the Bahamas in a couple of 
days. This system could acquire some subtropical characteristics 
late this week while it drifts over the western Atlantic. The 
chances of subtropical development should end by the weekend when 
the system is expected to move eastward or northeastward into 
unfavorable environmental conditions.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.
